title: backlog.py run by its full path from a host project reads the plugin's own backlog.json, and the plugin's skills and brief show no --root (second-project run)
goal: A backlog.py command a host project's session runs by the plugin's full path, from the host's working tree, reads the host's backlog.json and item directory (the root is the working tree's repository, or the skills and the brief pass --root), so no host command reads or writes the kb's own backlog

run: import os,subprocess,sys,tempfile; d=tempfile.mkdtemp(); subprocess.run(['git','init','-q',d]); o=subprocess.run([sys.executable,os.path.abspath('_tools/backlog.py'),'config'],cwd=d,capture_output=True,text=True).stdout; sys.exit(1 if 'kb/_self/backlog' in o else 0)

gates.question: How does a backlog.py command a host project runs by the plugin path find the host root?
options: default root is the working tree git top level whenever the tool runs from outside it
the skills and the brief pass --root on every command
gates.recommendation: default root is the working tree git top level whenever the tool runs from outside it

notes: Run finding 1: python3 <plugin>/_tools/backlog.py config in the host printed item_dir = "kb/_self/backlog"  (file); the orchestrator and the reviewer added --root to every command; the reviewer without it got no item ST-... A host worker's gate add without --root would write into the kb's backlog. Review gap 6 of SP-ciqk6gt6 (same cause): with no --root, a tool root that holds .git is its own root (bl_cli.default_root), so with --plugin-dir <kb clone> a host's backlog.json hooks key is never read and the plugin's horizon --hook --opt-in stays silent in the host. Blocks the Nerthus workspace adoption (BG-42dg5ryi's host); raised to P1 by the operator. Not planned into a sprint: the goal leaves a choice open (default_root takes the working tree's repository, or the skills and the brief pass --root) and every route touches an agents-rule path (_tools/bl_cli.py:126 default_root, which returns the tool root when it holds .git, so a --plugin-dir kb clone wins over the host's toplevel; or the plugin's skills/ and the brief), so rules backlog.md Dependencies want a blocking operator gate before code. Ran the repro as filed: python3 _tools/backlog.py config from a fresh git-init dir exits 0 and prints item_dir = "kb/_self/backlog"  (file), so it fails for the stated reason and stays as filed. Referrers of default_root: _tools/backlog.py:402 only; of root_of: backlog.py:402 and _tools/kb_mcp.py:283. Docs map: kb/_self/backlog.md and kb/_self/tools.md map to _tools/backlog.py. Next: add a design gate (default_root prefers the cwd's toplevel, or --root in skills and brief), then plan touches.
